verdict.line: You lose if you swing early and eat a Q (The Darkin Blade) reset chain into Umbral Dash disengage; you win if E (Test of Spirit) lands while his E (Umbral Dash) is down, since that's a trade he can't escape.

brief.thesis: The entire matchup is a cooldown race between your E (Test of Spirit), which locks a target in place and spawns a Vessel if they can't break line of sight, and his E (Umbral Dash), which is his only way to dodge it. His E is up far more often (9/8/7/6/5s) than yours is (16/15/14/13/12s), so you only get a handful of true E attempts per level — but when you land one while his dash is on cooldown, he is stuck trading into a tentacle swarm with no escape. This is why Illaoi holds both the lane win rate (52.8% over 36 games) and the solo-kill edge.

theirWindow.what: He can dash in to land Q (The Darkin Blade) or W (Infernal Chains) and then dash back out before your E lands, healing off the passive on Umbral Dash and Deathbringer Stance the whole time. Don't commit E here — you'll just whiff and lose the 16-12s cooldown for nothing.

yourWindow.when: he just used E to engage or reposition
yourWindow.what: Fire E (Test of Spirit) immediately. He has no dash to break it, so he either tanks the echo damage and stands still, or runs and becomes a Vessel — either way your passive Tentacles start swinging and healing you through the follow-up trade.

start.why: 51.7% win rate and the most-picked start (64.4%) — the extra sustain and damage let you hold position for W (Harsh Lesson) pokes without losing the trade war.

boots.why: 76.2% pick rate and best in this matchup — his damage is almost entirely physical autos and Q swings, including the Deathbringer Stance empowered auto, so flat physical reduction blunts his whole kit.

core.why: First item in the 100%-win, 3-game sample path — the armor shred compounds with every E echo and tentacle hit, letting you out-trade his healing.
Second in that same build path — the proc off W (Harsh Lesson) lets you stick to him after his E dash instead of losing the follow-up.
Caps the core path — the shield and tenacity-adjacent survivability keep you alive through his Q-W all-in windows while your tentacles do the real work.

runes.keystoneWhy: The 52.6%-win, most-picked page — Grasp rewards you for staying in minion range to farm tentacle procs and land W (Harsh Lesson), building the health lead that lets you ignore his poke until E is live.

summoners.why: Highest win rate of the three recorded combos (53.8%) — Ignite directly counters the healing from his passive Deathbringer Stance and Umbral Dash, and secures the kill once your E (Test of Spirit) traps him.

playing.title: Fight next to walls
playing.detail: Your passive Tentacles only spawn on nearby impassible terrain, so every trade you force should happen with a wall in tentacle range (W/E range, 400/900) or your damage output is half of what it should be.

playing.title: Hold E until his E is down
playing.detail: Umbral Dash cycles every 9-5s versus your Test of Spirit's 16-12s. Casting E into an up dash just wastes your longest cooldown — wait for him to spend it first.

playing.title: Watch his Deathbringer Stance charge
playing.detail: When his passive is armed, his next auto deals bonus magic damage and heals him off your max health. Back off a step or trade through it with your own W rather than absorbing a free empowered hit.

playing.title: Chip with W every 4 seconds
playing.detail: Harsh Lesson's 4s cooldown is far shorter than anything he has — use it on cooldown to proc nearby Tentacles even when E isn't up, keeping constant pressure without committing your long cooldowns.

playing.title: Punish a whiffed third Q swing
playing.detail: The Darkin Blade has three charges with different areas; if he burns all three without connecting, he's defenseless until it resets (14-6s) — this is your all-in window with W plus Tentacles.

playing.title: Save R for grouped minions
playing.detail: Leap of Faith spawns a Tentacle for every champion it hits, so timing it over a minion wave with Aatrox nearby builds an instant tentacle army for the all-in rather than a lone poke.

playing.title: Itemize into his sustain early
playing.detail: If he's out-healing your trades by level 9-13, prioritize Bramble Vest or Death's Dance from the situational list over pure damage — his Q/E healing scales hard and standard builds won't out-race it alone.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from real games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the cooldown-race reading, trade timing, and positioning calls are this brief's own tactical judgement.

stats.opponentTip: Aatrox is a difficult matchup as he can easily dodge [E] through (E) while dealing damage with (Q), not to mention his health regeneration or abilities that do not consume mana. However, Illaoi can gain the upper hand if [E] lands while (E) is on cooldown.
